claim_boundary: This evidence proves pure deterministic development-harness decision logic only. It proves no crash-safe persistence, supervisor, distributed consensus, command completion, security sandboxing, autonomous self-improvement or Raisa runtime capability.

covered_positive_decisions.note: A previously unseen command id is admitted as the first received event in the current generation.
An exact byte-bound repeat of a completed command returns its recorded result digest and nothing else.
A differing request under the same command id is a terminal conflict and is never admitted.
A live received or running command returns already_in_progress and never auto-replays.
Failed, revoked and uncertain commands never auto-replay and require a new immutable generation.
Recovery advances the journal generation exactly once and marks unfinished prior-generation work uncertain without executing it.
A same-generation cursor receives only later events in that generation.
A same-generation cursor at the latest sequence is up to date with no later events.
No prior attempt or any changed fingerprint component returns run_gate.
An exact prior deterministic pass is reused only for the identical bound candidate, evidence and manifest.
An exact prior deterministic failure returns diagnose_without_rerun and is never relabelled successful.
An exact prior uncertain result returns resolve_uncertainty and is never treated as a substantive failure or success.
Every new refinement proposal begins quarantined and the proposer cannot promote it.
Local promotion passes with a deterministic validation pass, exact bindings and a distinct Sol promotion authority.
Global promotion passes only with an additional distinct independent review pass.
Rejection is a first-class terminal decision record and edits or executes nothing.
Rollback creates a new immutable generation and names the exact promoted decision and its recorded base digest.

fail_closed_boundaries.note: A running command never returns replay_completed.
An uncertain command never returns replay_completed and is never silently re-executed.
A completed event without an exact result digest is rejected.
A non-completed event carrying a result digest is rejected.
A command whose first event is not received is rejected.
received to uncertain without a generation advance is rejected.
A generation whose sequences are not contiguous from one is rejected.
A retired-generation cursor returns snapshot_required.
A future-generation cursor returns snapshot_required.
A cursor pointing into a sequence gap returns snapshot_required.
An out-of-range cursor returns snapshot_required.
A command whose request digest changes across events is rejected.
A differing request under an existing command id is conflict in every live or terminal state.
A reordered event array is rejected even when its coordinates could be sorted into validity.
A retired-generation received or running command without its recovery uncertainty is rejected.
A gate fingerprint missing any composite component is rejected.
Transient/provider/transport/timeout outcomes can only be represented as uncertain.
A pass is reused only for identical candidate/evidence/manifest fingerprints.
No gate decision executes the gate or converts a failure/uncertainty into success.
Duplicate attempt identity/generation or conflicting results for one exact fingerprint fail closed rather than using latest-wins.
Closed non-executable kinds and bounded text/digest fields make code, commands, dependencies and credentials unrepresentable.
A promotion where the promoter equals the proposer is rejected.
Promotion requires a validation manifest digest exactly equal to the proposal.
A proposal without bounded source-evidence digests is rejected.
A promotion whose base-state binding differs from the proposal is rejected.
Independent review by the proposer or the promoter is rejected.
Global promotion without a distinct independent review pass is rejected.
In-place history rewriting is rejected; generations and decisions are append-only.
Rollback must name exactly one promoted decision and its recorded base digest.
Promotion binds the canonical proposal digest, exact source HEAD and exact source-evidence digests.
Promotion and rollback require exact Sol authority; a generic non-proposer identity is insufficient.
Unknown, repeated, intervened or current-state-mismatched rollback targets fail closed.
Decision histories require unique ordered generations and each new proposal uses the exact next generation.
Promotion emits only a typed decision record and never edits a policy, prompt, skill or source file.
